text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- National police chief says Nigeria seeks access to Britain to investigate a spate of bombings which military government says are masterminded by its exiled opponents. Eleven dissidents, including exiled Nobel Laureate Wole Soyinka, have been charged in connection with the bombings.
- National Insurance Corp of Nigeria wins court battle to be sole insurer for state-owned Nigerian National Oil Corp.
- Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi satisfied with organisation of weekend local elections; says foreign critics of Nigeria's military government disappointed.

- African-American elections monitoring delegation hails commitment of Nigerians to democracy; pledges to try to convince West that Nigeria's military government is sincere about restoring civilian rule.

- Police from special fraud unit arrest and detain Bashir Tofa, northern politician who was the rival of jailed presidential claimant Moshood Abiola in 1993 elections; military rulers scrapped poll results as Abiola headed for victory.

- Airlines differ on new domestic air fares; State-owned Nigeria Airways raises its fares by about 65 percent while private carriers hike theirs by the full 100 percent they were authorised to charge.
- Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corp starts in-house training on how to liquidate failed banks.

- Weak Naira portends hard times for all, say bankers; paper reproduces transcript of a roundtable it organised to assess this month's depreciation of the Naira from 80 to the U.S. dollar to 85 to the dollar.

- Nigeria may send detectives to Britain and the United States for investigations into terrorist acts blamed on exiled opponents; diplomats say military government will face uphill tasks if it comes to extradition of fugitive Nigerians.
- Petitions flood offices of the National Elections Commission after Saturday's nationwide local elections.
